Consider the diagram shown above, where $\overset{\to }{AE}=a,$ $\overset{\to }{DB}=b,$ $\overset{\to }{CB}=c,$ and $\overset{\to }{AD}=d.$ Find $\overset{\to }{EC}$ in terms of  $a,b,c,$ and $d.$ To denote the corresponding vectors, use $a$, $b,$ $c,$ and $d.$

$\overset{\to }{EC}=$   
 {{field-1}}
question.worked_solution:
We want to find a "path" from $E$ to $C$ consisting only of the vectors $a,b,c,$ and $d.$

According to the triangle law of addition,

$$
\overset{\to }{EC}=\overset{\to }{EA}+\overset{\to }{AD}+\overset{\to }{DB}+\overset{\to }{BC}
$$

as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/a8b76bf9fc26742d8ba05c962e59986e9f7b596f0b02c8e71c4ead4b45cf542a.png)

 

Now, from the original diagram, we have that

$$
\overset{\to }{EA}=-a,\,\overset{\to }{AD}=d,\,\overset{\to }{DB}=b,\,\overset{\to }{BC}=-c.
$$

Let's add these to our diagram.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14212914/assets/fe663b4bfacc4ef2078e014af664e99123cb803fd26d03a449bf9bf6198629cc.png)

 

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{EC} & =\overset{\to }{EA}+\overset{\to }{AD}+\overset{\to }{DB}+\overset{\to }{BC} \\  & =-a+d+b+(-c) \\  & =-a+d+b-c.\end{aligned}
$$
